Gnosis Interpretation
MOVE is Treasury volatility and term-premium stress: below 80 is calm, 80-120 is moderate uncertainty, and 150+ is high stress. At 98.47, rate volatility remains moderate. SOFR is secured overnight funding; its 1 bp dip alone does not establish funding stress or its absence. NFCI at -0.494 signals looser-than-average broad financial conditions, slightly less loose than the prior week. The 10Y yield rose 2 bp to 5.24%.

Fed & Policy Watch
  • Columbus Day is a Federal Reserve holiday. The Board says daily and weekly releases scheduled for today shift to Tuesday, Oct 13. The Board lists Beige Book at 2:00 PM ET; Chicago Fed's data-release calendar lists 3:00 PM ET. Using the Board's publisher calendar time, with the conflict disclosed.
  • Federal Reserve releases this week include the Beige Book and statistical releases; a Board Governor discussion is scheduled Tuesday at 3:45 AM ET. Check the exact calendar rows above.
  • Treasury's Oct 13 bill supply is $95B 13-week, $82B 26-week (both competitive cutoff 11:30 AM ET), and $95B 6-week (1:00 PM ET). Auctions are distinct from coupon issuance; the three bills issue Oct 15.
Omissions and Watch
  • Conflict check covered BLS, BEA, Census, TreasuryDirect, EIA, the Federal Reserve Board, New York/Chicago/Philadelphia Fed calendars, NAR, NYSE, SIFMA and CME. No timed macro release remains today. Past releases were removed.
  • BLS automated direct requests returned HTTP 403. Official BLS pages were inspected via web access; CPI is Oct 14, PPI is Oct 15, and import/export prices are Oct 16, each at 8:30 AM ET. CPI and PPI are separate events. BEA has no release in this week-ahead window; its next listed macro releases are Oct 29.
  • New York Fed's Empire State survey is dated Oct 15, but its official page gives publication as "at or shortly after 8:30" rather than an exact time; omitted under the exact-time rule. TreasuryDirect's confirmed Oct 13 auctions are included; later auctions without final dated notices are omitted rather than inferred.
  • Chicago Beige Book calendar conflicts with the Board on time (3:00 PM vs 2:00 PM ET); the Board is the release publisher and its 2:00 PM time is used. Chicago Fed NFCI's next scheduled release is Oct 15 at 8:30 AM ET, reference week ending Oct 9.
  • Michigan preliminary sentiment was released Oct 9 and is omitted as elapsed. NYSE is scheduled open Oct 12, while SIFMA recommends a fixed-income close and the Fed and U.S. repo market are closed. CME holiday session hours apply; CME reports settlement prices at normal times. Verify product-specific hours before trading.
  • Waller's AI discussion, final Chicago CARTS, the scheduled NFCI update and G.17 are provisional Medium from the classifier and carry review notes. No unverified geopolitical or policy headline is promoted to a timed event.
  • Current quote APIs did not provide live holiday prices or complete timestamps for all markets; the snapshot is delayed and single-source. Unverified prices/times are not invented.
Trading Strategy Note | ES Futures
BASE CASE
Columbus Day splits market liquidity: NYSE cash is scheduled to open, but fixed income and U.S. repo are closed and CME holiday hours apply. Expect less confirmation from rates plumbing; avoid treating stale Friday closes as a Monday signal. The next major repricing catalysts are Wednesday CPI and Thursday retail sales/PPI. Scenario framework only, not a trade signal.
INVALIDATION
Reassess if ES sustains a range break with confirmation from live yields, volatility and market depth, or if trading hours differ for the contract. No unsupported levels or price targets are supplied; reconfirm live quotes before execution.
